premises.text: Plastics are a huge polluting waste stream but also a $600B enabling industry that will not disappear
premises.evidence_span: They're a $600 billion industry, so they're not going away anytime soon

premises.text: Recycling and industrial composting are fragmented, slow, or unavailable, so enzymes must work inside the plastic
premises.evidence_span: Recycling is great when it works, but it's fragmented, complex, it's laborious, the margins are low

premises.text: Proprietary coating lets enzymes be embedded in plastics and triggered to degrade from the inside out
premises.evidence_span: special proprietary coating that acts like PPE and enables us to take these fragile molecules and put them inside the plastics, where they can be triggered to degrade the materials from the inside out

premises.text: Materials return to soil; warm-water baths offer scalable infrastructure and optional chemical recycling
premises.evidence_span: they completely return to the soil at the end of life. We can also break them down and warm water baths

premises.text: End-to-end degradation engineering stops microplastics at the source
premises.evidence_span: we're able to degrade from one end to the other through some clever engineering work that we were able to do, which means we stop microplastics at the source

premises.text: Drop-in, low-dose, water-and-heat-triggered additive is readily scalable
